title: Roast Potatoes
subtitle: Crisp, fluffy roast potatoes in goose or duck fat
excerpt: Floury potatoes parboiled, roughed up, and roasted in very hot fat until the exterior is shatteringly crisp and the interior is fluffy and light. The perfect British Sunday roast side.

recipe.sourceNotes: The perfect roast potato is the subject of more debate in Britain than almost any other cooking question. There are several firmly held principles: the potato must be a floury variety (Maris Piper, King Edward, or Desiree) because waxy potatoes do not fluff up on the inside; the potatoes must be parboiled so the edges soften and create a rough surface that will crisp in the fat; the fat must be very hot before the potatoes go in; and the potatoes must have sufficient space in the tin to roast rather than steam. The choice of fat is also debated: goose fat and duck fat produce the most flavourful and crisp results; lard is also excellent; vegetable oil works well but produces a slightly less golden result. Parboiling in salted water, then shaking the drained potatoes vigorously in the pan to roughen the edges, is the technique that creates the characteristic craggy exterior.

recipeTools.notes: A large roasting tin, not too deep.

content.text: Two things are non-negotiable: the fat must be smoking hot before the potatoes go in, and the potatoes must have enough space not to crowd each other. Crowded potatoes steam; spaced potatoes roast. Do not turn the potatoes more than twice during roasting: each turn must produce a new, clearly golden surface before the potato is flipped again.

items.preparation: Maris Piper or King Edward, peeled and cut into even chunks
or goose fat or duck fat

content.text: Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Put the fat in the roasting tin and heat in the oven for 15 minutes until smoking hot. Parboil the potatoes in well-salted boiling water for 7 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Return the drained potatoes to the dry pan and shake vigorously with the lid on for 15 to 20 seconds until the edges are roughened and fluffy. Season with salt.

Carefully lower the potatoes into the hot fat in the tin: they should sizzle immediately. Toss to coat. Add the garlic and rosemary if using. Roast for 50 to 55 minutes, turning twice, until deeply golden and crisp all over. Season with a final pinch of salt and serve immediately.
